title: Store submission and compliance
summary: Two stores, one restricted-permission review, and an honest listing
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing submitted. No developer accounts confirmed.

APPLE: a Call Directory extension and an SMS filter extension are ordinary app extensions and need no special entitlement — verified, they are plain NSExtension points in the public SDK. (The one Apple approval this project would have needed, Live Caller ID Lookup, is out of scope.) Needs signing and provisioning for the app plus both extension targets, and an App Group.

GOOGLE PLAY — THE ONLY LAUNCH DEPENDENCY OUTSIDE OUR CONTROL: the SMS and Call Log permission groups are restricted. A Permissions Declaration and review are required. Caller ID and spam blocking is understood to be a permitted use case, so there is a legitimate path, but approval is not guaranteed. FILE EARLY — it runs in parallel with development rather than after it. Confirm current policy and process in T002. If refused, Android SMS filtering cannot ship and the listing and app must adapt.

HUAWEI APPGALLERY: a third submission, no Google services. Currently "possibly" — confirm before anyone designs for it. Older EMUI devices run the Android build as-is.

THE LISTING MUST NOT OVERPROMISE. R2's honesty requirement applies outward too, and this category's app-store reviews are full of users who felt misled. Specifically, the listing must not imply that on iPhone the app can:
- tell you it blocked a call (it cannot — no callback exists)
- let you block the number that just called you (it cannot — no call history API)
- apply very broad rules such as a whole country or a large city to calls (it cannot — those exceed the entry limit)
None of these are defects; all three are Apple platform limits. Saying so plainly costs less than a one-star review saying it does not work.

Screenshots and copy differ per platform because the products genuinely differ. Do not reuse Android screenshots showing an activity log or one-tap block on the iOS listing.
